threads.thread_goal: Align on current-state mapping and target payroll workflow design.

messages.text:
Kicking off this thread to map how we currently run payroll and related documents, so we can converge on a single standard flow for Standardise Payroll and Office Documentation Workflow.
I have started T1 with a draft list of steps from data collection to payment confirmation, but it is still rough.
Can everyone share briefly how they handle: 1) absence and overtime inputs, 2) approvals, 3) last checks before we send the payment file?
Once we align, we will turn this into the official sequence in A1 and then build the monthly checklist in T3 on top of it.

Thanks for starting this.
My current flow looks like this:
1) I receive absence and overtime details by email or in a shared folder, usually in different formats.
2) I key them into the payroll file and cross check with last month for anything unusual.
3) I calculate gross, then taxes and contributions, and prepare a draft summary.
4) I send the summary to finance for a quick review and only then generate the payment file.
I do not have a formal checklist, so I am keen that T3 captures all these points.
Happy to adjust my steps to match what others are doing.

On my side, I usually start from the bank statement and then work backwards.
I check last month wages, then update for any new hires or leavers, and only after that I look at overtime and absences.
I also recalculate taxes manually in a separate sheet to see if the totals look right.
I am not sure if this is the best order, but it is how I have been doing it.
Maybe we can just say the official flow is: bank statement, then wages, then absences and overtime, then taxes?

From the office side, I see three main touchpoints:
1) Staff bring paper forms or send emails for absences and overtime.
2) We log them and route to the right payroll clerk.
3) We answer basic questions from staff about when changes will show in their pay.
Right now, routing is inconsistent, which is why T2 and T4 are important.
For this thread, I think we should agree that the payroll flow starts when we receive validated inputs from us, not when the bank statement arrives.
That will make A1 easier to read and connect better with the future document routing rules.

Adding to that, when staff hand in forms at the front desk, I usually just put them in a tray labelled payroll and someone picks them up later.
Sometimes I email a scan, sometimes not.
I am not sure at which exact point this should appear in the official sequence.
Should we say that the first step is intake at the front desk, or is that part of the document routing work in another thread?

Good question.
For A1, I suggest we start the payroll workflow at the point where validated data reaches payroll, and we reference the intake and routing steps but detail them in the document routing guideline.
So the early steps would be:
1) Receive validated absence and overtime data from office clerks.
2) Update payroll input sheet with changes in staff, rates, and hours.
3) Run calculations and generate draft totals.
4) Perform checks and reconciliations.
5) Get approvals.
6) Generate payment file and confirm with bank.
We can still show that office intake happens before step 1, but keep the detailed routing in A3 later.
Does that sound workable?

This matches how I would like to see it.
I would only add an explicit step for tax and contribution checks before approvals, so that T3 can list them clearly.
Maybe:
3) Run calculations.
4) Check taxes and contributions.
5) Reconcile totals with previous month and budget.
6) Get approvals.
If we agree on that, I can help fill in T3 with due dates relative to pay day.

I see the logic.
I had been starting from the bank statement mostly for my own checks, but for a standard flow it makes sense to start from the inputs.
I would still like to keep a step where we compare the final totals to the bank statement after the payment file is processed, maybe as a final confirmation.
Could we add a last step like: confirm payments posted correctly in the bank and log any discrepancies?

From the office side, I am fine with the payroll flow starting at the point where we hand over validated data.
To keep the link clear, we can note in A1 that step 1 depends on the document routing rules that we will define in A3 and T4.
That way, when we train clerks later, they can see how their part feeds into the payroll steps.
No changes needed from me on the sequence you proposed, plus the extra checks suggested in the last messages.

Understood.
So for now I will just make sure that when I pass on forms, they are complete and clearly labelled, and we will detail the earlier steps in the other thread.
For this one, I agree that the official flow can start when payroll receives the validated data.
I do not have anything else to add on the sequence.

Summarising what we have so far for the standard payroll workflow in A1:
1) Receive validated absence and overtime data from office clerks.
2) Update payroll input sheet with staff changes and hours.
3) Run payroll calculations.
4) Check taxes and contributions.
5) Reconcile totals with previous month and budget.
6) Obtain approvals from finance or management as required.
7) Generate payment file and submit to bank.
8) Confirm payments posted correctly in the bank and log discrepancies.
If no one objects, I will record this as the official sequence for D1 and reflect it in T1 and T3.

Looks good to me.
For role ownership, I suggest:
1) Office clerks.
2) Payroll clerks.
3) Payroll clerks.
4) Payroll clerks.
5) Payroll clerks with finance support.
6) Finance manager or delegate.
7) Payroll clerks.
8) Payroll clerks with finance for the bank confirmation.
This should be enough to close D2 if everyone agrees.

I am fine with that split.
On step 5, I can take the lead on the reconciliation with budget and previous month, and then share the summary with finance.
That way the finance manager only needs to review the final numbers before approving.
No further changes from my side.

Agree on the ownership list.
For step 1, we can later break down which office clerk handles which department in the document routing work, but for A1 it is enough to say office clerks.
This will also help when we prepare the training outline and quick reference guides.

Works for me.
Once the routing rules are clearer, I will adjust how I log and pass on forms so that step 1 runs smoothly.
Nothing else to add on roles.

Thanks all.
I will update A1 and T1 with the agreed sequence and role ownership and start drafting T3 based on these steps.
We can refine details when we prepare the checklist, but for now D1 and D2 are covered so we can move on to routing and templates in the next thread.

threads.thread_goal: Define document routing, archiving structure, and templates.

messages.text:
Starting the routing and templates thread.
I have drafted initial document routing rules in T4 and a first version of the absence and overtime template for T2.
The idea is to connect front desk intake to the payroll steps we agreed in A1, and to align with the archiving structure in A3.
Please review and share what might be missing, especially around urgent items and who should receive which forms.

Quick summary of the routing proposal in T4:
- Standard items: front desk logs the form, scans it, saves it in the shared folder following A3 naming rules, and routes it to the generic payroll inbox.
- Urgent items (for the current payroll cut off): same as above, plus a short email to the payroll inbox with 'urgent' in the subject.
- Queries from staff: logged and routed to the payroll inbox, with a note on expected response time.
For templates in T2, I added fields for employee id, dates, hours, type of absence or overtime, and manager approval.
Let me know if any fields are missing from a payroll perspective.

I like the idea of having clear urgent vs standard rules.
One thing I am not sure about is how to handle forms that arrive by post.
Right now I just put them in the same tray as walk in forms.
Should we treat them as standard items unless the sender marks them as urgent, or do we need a different rule?

From payroll side, the fields you listed for T2 cover most of what we need.
I would add:
- Cost centre or department, so we can reconcile with budgets.
- Indicator if the change affects previous periods, so we know if an adjustment is needed.
For routing, sending everything to a generic payroll inbox works, as long as we can still see who logged the item in case we have questions.
Maybe add a field in the log for the clerk who handled intake.

Agree with the suggestions so far.
For urgent items, could we also define a cut off time in T4, for example anything received after a certain hour automatically moves to the next cycle unless a manager explicitly approves an exception?
That will help us avoid last minute manual changes that are hard to track in A2 later.

On the template in T2, could we include a field for hourly rate or salary reference, or is that too sensitive for the form?
If we do not include it, we need to be sure we can easily match the form to the correct rate in the system.
Also, for archiving in A3, I suggest we use a naming convention like year month type employee id, so that reconciliations are easier later.

For post, I would treat them as standard unless clearly marked urgent.
We can add a note in T4 that if a posted form is close to the cut off date, the clerk should flag it as urgent when logging it.
I will also add a field in the log for the intake clerk, as suggested.
On the template, I prefer not to include salary figures, but we can require employee id and department so payroll can look up the rate.

Got it.
I will start marking late arriving post as urgent in the log when it is close to cut off.
Once T4 is final, I will keep it open on my screen when handling mail so I follow the same steps every time.

I support having a clear cut off time.
Maybe we can say in T4 that urgent items for the current cycle must be logged and routed by noon on the cut off day, otherwise they move to the next cycle unless finance approves an exception.
We can then reflect that timing in the monthly checklist in A4 so it is consistent.

Noon on cut off day works for me.
If we get anything after that, we can log it in A2 for the next cycle and note that it missed the cut off.
That will also help when we review issues after the pilot in A7.

Agree on the cut off and on not including salary figures in the template.
As long as employee id and department are mandatory fields in T2, we can link to the correct rate.
For archiving in T7, I will follow the naming convention you suggested so that payroll reports line up with the folders.

Let me summarise the routing rules for D3 based on this discussion:
- All forms and emails are logged by the intake clerk with date, time, employee id, department, and whether they are urgent.
- Standard items are scanned and saved using the A3 naming convention, then routed to the generic payroll inbox.
- Urgent items for the current cycle must be logged and routed by noon on cut off day, plus an email with 'urgent' in the subject.
- Items received after the cut off move to the next cycle unless finance approves an exception.
- Posted items follow the same rules; if they arrive close to cut off, the clerk marks them urgent in the log.
If there are no objections, I will mark these as the approved routing rules in T4 and A3.

Summary looks good.
For the templates in T2, I propose we finalise the absence and overtime form with these mandatory fields: employee id, department, dates, hours, type of absence or overtime, manager approval, and indicator if it affects previous periods.
Cost centre can be optional if it matches department.
If everyone agrees, we can treat this as the final version for D4 and use it in the quick reference guide A6 and T9.

I am comfortable using that template.
Having clear mandatory fields will make it easier at the front desk to check forms before we log them.
No further changes from me.

Template fields work for payroll.
With employee id and department, we can link to rates and cost centres on our side.
I will make sure the monthly checklist in A4 references the routing cut off and the use of this template.

No objections from me on D3 and D4.
Once T7 is updated with the folder structure and examples, I will test a couple of months of data to see if the routing and archiving work smoothly together.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in confidentiality, access levels, and escalation paths.

messages.text:
Opening the confidentiality and escalation thread.
I have drafted a first version of the confidentiality and access guideline in T6, and a basic escalation path for discrepancies in T11.
These will feed into A5 and A8.
Please review and share any concerns, especially around who can see what, and how we handle wage or hours discrepancies raised by staff.

In T6, I see three access levels proposed:
1) Full access for payroll clerks and HR to detailed payroll records.
2) Limited access for office clerks to routing logs and high level status only.
3) Read only access for finance to summaries and reconciliations.
This makes sense to me, but we should be explicit that office clerks should not open or store files with full salary details unless strictly needed for routing.
Maybe we can add a rule that any such files are handled only by payroll or HR.

I agree with the three access levels.
For A5, we should also cover how long we keep documents and where backups are stored.
For example, detailed payroll records kept for a set number of years in the secure archive, and logs in A2 kept for a shorter period.
On escalation in T11, I would like to see clear response times, such as two working days for initial response and five working days for resolution where possible.

From the office side, I support limiting access to detailed salary data.
We mainly need to see whether a form has been received, logged, and processed, not the actual amounts.
In A6 and the training outline, we can emphasise that any documents with full pay details should be sealed or marked confidential and passed directly to payroll without copying.

That helps.
Sometimes staff hand me envelopes with payslips or letters from external agencies.
I was not always sure if I should open them.
With this guideline, I will treat anything marked confidential as for payroll or HR only and just log that I passed it on, without opening it.

On retention, I can add to T6 that:
- Detailed payroll records are stored in the secure archive for the required number of years.
- Routing logs and issue logs in A2 and A7 are kept for a shorter period, enough to support audits and reviews.
For escalation in T11, I propose three scenarios: incorrect hours, incorrect rate, and missing payment.
Each would have an initial response within two working days and target resolution within five working days, with clear contacts at each step.

For the escalation path in T11, I suggest this order:
1) Staff contact office clerk or payroll inbox.
2) Office clerk logs the query in A2 and forwards to payroll.
3) Payroll reviews and, if needed, escalates to HR or finance.
4) If not resolved within the target time, it goes to the finance manager.
We should also note in A8 that any adjustments after payroll close must be documented and, where needed, approved by finance before processing.

That sequence works.
I would only add that for missing payments, we should check the bank file and confirmation step in A1 before assuming an error in the payroll calculation.
If the payment was rejected by the bank, the escalation should include contacting the bank or finance to resolve it.

From the office perspective, it is helpful to have clear response times and to know when to follow up.
In A6, we can include a short section explaining to clerks how to log queries in A2 and when to escalate if staff come back asking for updates.

Yes, having that written down will help a lot.
Right now I sometimes promise staff I will check and then I am not sure who to ask.
With A8 and the log in A2, I can follow the same steps every time.

Let me summarise the confidentiality and access rules for D5:
- Payroll clerks and HR have full access to detailed payroll records.
- Office clerks have access only to routing logs and high level status, not to detailed salary data, except when strictly needed for routing.
- Finance has read only access to summaries and reconciliations.
- Documents marked confidential are passed directly to payroll or HR without being opened by office clerks.
- Retention periods are defined for detailed records and logs, with storage in secure archives.
If everyone is aligned, I will update T6 and A5 accordingly.

I am aligned with that summary.
For D6, I suggest we formalise the escalation path in A8 and T11 as:
1) Staff raise discrepancy via office clerk or payroll inbox.
2) Office clerk logs it in A2 and forwards to payroll.
3) Payroll investigates and, if needed, involves HR or finance.
4) If not resolved within five working days, it escalates to the finance manager.
5) Any adjustments after payroll close are documented and approved by finance before processing.
If there are no objections, we can treat this as the agreed standard path.

No objections from me on D5 and D6.
I will make sure the monthly checklist in A4 includes a step to review open discrepancies in A2 before we close payroll.

All good from the office side.
I will reflect the confidentiality rules and escalation steps in the training outline in T12 and in the quick reference guide A6 so clerks know exactly what to do.

I am clear on the rules and the escalation path now.
I will start logging staff queries in A2 as described and follow the steps in A8 when people come to the desk with concerns about their pay.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare and execute the pilot payroll cycle using the new workflow.

messages.text:
Time to plan the pilot payroll cycle using the new workflow.
We need to confirm which cycle we will use for the pilot and what success looks like.
I have started T8 with a draft plan and updated T5 with a first version of the shared tracking sheet that links to A2.
Please confirm readiness and share any concerns before we lock in dates.

Thanks for setting this up.
I propose we use the next monthly payroll cycle as the pilot, not the current one, so we have enough time to brief office clerks and finalise A4 and A5.
For success criteria, I suggest: all steps in A4 completed on time, all inputs logged in A2 using the new routing rules, and any issues captured in A7.

I agree that we should not use the current cycle, as deadlines are tight.
Using the next monthly cycle gives us time to align invoice issuing in T10 with the new document workflow as well.
For success, I would add that reconciliations should match without extra manual work, and that any discrepancies follow the escalation path in A8.

From the office side, the next monthly cycle works.
We can use the time before then to walk through the routing rules in T4, the templates in T2, and the quick reference guide A6 with clerks.
For success, I would like to see that all forms in the pilot period are handled using the new routing and that clerks feel comfortable with the process.

I am ok with using the next cycle.
I will need a short walkthrough of the tracking sheet in T5 and how to log items in A2, but once I see it in action I should be fine.
No concerns on timing from me.

So far, everyone seems aligned on using the next monthly cycle.
Unless there are objections, we can record that as D7.
For success criteria under D8, I like the points mentioned: checklist completion, proper use of A2, reconciliations without extra manual work, and issues logged in A7.
We should also track how many urgent items miss the cut off, to see if the routing rules are realistic.

Agreed on D7.
For D8, I suggest we define success as:
- 100 percent of steps in A4 completed and ticked off in T5.
- All payroll related forms in the pilot period logged in A2 with correct fields.
- All discrepancies handled using the escalation path in A8 and recorded in A7.
- No breaches of the confidentiality rules in A5.
If we meet these, we can consider the pilot successful and move to full rollout.

Those criteria work for me.
On T10, I will map the touchpoints between invoices and payroll before the pilot starts, so that any invoice related items are also tracked in A2 and archived according to A3.
This will help us see the full picture when we review the pilot.

I am aligned on D7 and D8.
Before the pilot, I will finalise the training outline in T12 and run a short session with clerks to walk through T4, T2, A6, and the tracking sheet in T5.
During the pilot, I will also collect feedback from clerks on what works and what feels confusing so we can log it in A7.

Thanks, that training will help.
During the pilot I will make sure to log every form and query in A2 and follow the routing and escalation rules.
If I run into anything unclear, I will note it so it can go into A7 for the review.

To prepare for the pilot, I will:
- Finalise T5 so that it mirrors the steps in A4 and includes fields for owner and due date.
- Set up views in A2 to track inputs, approvals, and discrepancies.
- Create the initial A7 log structure so we can capture issues as they happen.
Once that is ready, we can do a quick dry run with a small set of test data before the real cycle.

Sounds good.
I will support with the dry run by entering sample data and checking that the checklist in A4 and the tracking in T5 and A2 line up.
During the actual pilot, I will also keep an eye on any confidentiality issues and note them in A7 if they occur.

During the pilot cycle, I will focus on reconciliations and on checking that invoice related steps in T10 integrate smoothly with the payroll workflow.
Any issues I find will be logged in A7 with suggestions for adjustments before full rollout.

After the pilot, I suggest we run a short retrospective using A7 as input: what worked, what did not, and what we want to change.
We can then update A3, A6, and T12 if needed before declaring the workflow final.

Agreed.
We now have D7 and D8 confirmed, and a clear set of preparation tasks.
I will update T8 with the chosen cycle, the success criteria, and the plan for the dry run and retrospective.
Let us use this thread to post quick status updates as we get closer to the pilot date.
